note: Every row edits the PRODUCER of a sentence, never the test. `shape` says which assertion the row is evidence for: `positive` rows delete the clause a match now names, `negation` rows make the producer emit BOTH confusable sentences so the doesNotMatch has something to fire on. The two must be counted separately. `baseline_ref` is the commit before the sweep, so each row also reports what the assertion it replaced did with the same injection — but that comparison is only meaningful on `positive` rows, because every pre-sweep site was an assert.match and none was a negation, so a `negation` row's old result is trivially a pass and is NOT evidence of anything.
